findings.title: L1 module custody ties band and at1 to one module, so an at1 successor after the Phase-1 freeze forces a band re-run with a new L1 sha (process, present since v003)
findings.evidence: at1 refuses any L1 whose module is not MODULE (A144 custody, adopted 0716). v003b refuses v003a-written L1s (T45(b) passes in my run). If an at1 successor is needed between the Phase-1 freeze (band, L1 sha logged per A133 1.6) and Phase-2 AT-1, it will refuse the logged v003b L1. Band would then have to be re-run under the successor; its rows would be identical except module (R01), but its L1 sha would differ from the logged one. Root may want to settle this before the seal, for example by having at1 accept a declared list of band-identical modules, or by a rule that a re-run L1 is logged next to the original.

findings.title: Where eps_km_s comes from (the member's own certificate, A152 srb_rot) is enforced only by the members writer; at1 requires the 43-entry list on member_valid=false points too
findings.evidence: at1 reads eps_km_s as given. check_member_eps enforces only that every member point of the file has a list of exactly 43 entries, including member_valid=false points (v003 CHOICE 5, adopted), and member_eps checks each entry. Nothing in at1 links the entries to the member's own certificate. The ruled requirement (A144 R3, 43 entries from the member's own point certificate; A152 W-3) therefore rests on the values/members writer: it must also emit a 43-entry list for failed-member points, or at1 refuses MEMBERS (fails closed, no out-dir). A cross-check for Claude4's values-writer review; not checkable from the named paths.
